claims: Ken Jennings holds the all-time Jeopardy! record with a 74-game winning streak in 2004.
Ken Jennings accumulated $2,520,700 in regular-season winnings.
Ken Jennings' historic run increased Jeopardy! show ratings by 22%.
Ken Jennings' historic run ended on November 30, 2004.
Ken Jennings' historic run ended after a loss to Nancy Zerg.
Ken Jennings later became a guest host of Jeopardy!.
Ken Jennings eventually became a permanent host of Jeopardy!.
Ken Jennings' 74-game streak duration was June 2, 2004 – November 30, 2004.
On his 75th appearance, Ken Jennings lost in Final Jeopardy to Nancy Zerg.
Nancy Zerg is a real estate agent from California.
The Final Jeopardy question was 'Most of this firm's 70,000 seasonal white-collar employees work only four months a year.'
Ken Jennings answered 'What is FedEx?' to the Final Jeopardy question.
The correct response to the Final Jeopardy question was 'What is H&R Block?'.
Jennings holds the longest winning streak in Jeopardy! history.
Amy Schneider holds second place with 40 wins.
During his run, Ken Jennings gave over 2,700 correct answers.
Ken Jennings won the Jeopardy! Greatest of All Time (GOAT) tournament.
Jeopardy! changed rules in 2003 that allowed contestants to stay on the show until they were defeated, rather than retiring after five wins.
